qt: to the Commission Nikos Pappas (The Left) Subject:

For many years now, Greece has faced serious zoonotic diseases that have had devastating consequences, especially for sheep and goat farming. Following the mass culls in the wake of the sheep and goat pox outbreak, thousands of holdings have been left with no productive livestock and the sector is unable to recover. Regulation (EU) 2020/687 provides for a monitoring period of 21 days for the repopulation of a holding after a pox outbreak, subject to certain health conditions. However, the Greek authorities are saying that, in Greece, repopulation is allowed six months after the last outbreak recorded in the country. Prolonged restrictions entail a risk of permanent abandonment of the sector, as well as making it virtually impossible to establish new holdings and include new livestock farmers in the Young Farmers programme. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

To what extent is the horizontal restriction of six months for the repopulation or establishment of new livestock holdings compatible with EU law, in particular when it is enforced without individual epidemiological assessments being carried out and goes beyond the requirements laid down in Regulation (EU) 2016/429 and the relevant EU framework?
How far can the national authorities go in imposing additional or stricter measures than those provided for in EU law?

Does it intend to ask the Greek authorities to review the existing framework and the application of a proportionate and science-based protocol for safe repopulation that takes individual epidemiological circumstances into account while ensuring the protection of young livestock farmers and beneficiaries of the Young Farmers programme?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2026) Sheep pox and goat pox (SPGP) control measures at EU level are laid down in Regulation (EU) 2016/4291 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/6872. Additional EU rules for control measures and movement restrictions for SPGP are laid down in Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/22073. These rules were prolonged in view of the uninterrupted, prolonged and geographically widespread virus circulation. The prohibition of restocking affected establishments in Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2024/2207 is a specific measure intended to halt further virus spread, designed to avoid increasing the number of ‘naïve/susceptible’ animals in the restricted zones in a situation where the SPGP virus has been circulating for a long time and over very wide areas. This measure should be therefore considered in the context of the specific emergency measures adopted for SPGP in Greece. It reflects the prohibition to enter animals into restricted zones laid down in Annex VI to Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2020/687 but limits the use of derogations under that Annex. National authorities may apply additional measures where justified by the epidemiological situation, provided that these comply with EU legislation and proportionate to the level of risk. The Commission follows closely the epidemiological situation in Greece and remains ready to discuss with the Greek competent authorities measures to be implemented in restricted zones, in particular the use of vaccination.
